# Windows and the Level 3 hooks

## 1. Git for Windows (Git Bash) is a prerequisite

U06 (fact) Level 3 ships the bash hooks and the git pre-commit hook only, with no PowerShell variants (decision D16) [D16, manifest 7-9].

        324: Windows (Git Bash), because the `Bash` matcher, the `if` field and the `Bash(...)` permission rules only apply when

U08 (fact) The Level 3 commit hook is a `PreToolUse` handler with the matcher `Bash` and the `if` rule `Bash(git commit *)`, and every permission rule that runs a command is a `Bash(...)` rule [settings 12-16, 21-24, 30, 34].
    [settings 12-16, 21-24, 30, 34] ok

        21: "Bash(git push)",

        24: "Bash(git commit -n *)"

## 2. A hook that cannot start blocks the commit

U15 (fact) The commit hook handler sets `"onFailure": "block"` [settings 36].
    [settings 36] ok
        36: "onFailure": "block",

U16 (fact) With it, Claude Code 2.1.295 or later blocks the commit when the hook cannot start, times out, or exits with any code other than 0 and 2 [E 26, E 29, E 35, Q3 964-972].
    [E 26] ok
        26: "a timed-out command , http , or mcp_tool hook doesn?t block the tool call, except for hooks whose failure blocks the action . The call continues through the normal permission flow , so don?t count on a stalled hook to act as a gate. To block the call when a command or http hook times out, set onFailure: "block" ."
    [E 29] ok
        29: "Unless the hook is one whose failure blocks the action , a hook that can?t start is a non-blocking error too. When you set up a policy hook, watch for this notice on its first run, because a mistyped path in settings.json means the hook never runs. To block the action when the hook can?t start, set onFailure: "block" ."
    [E 35] ok
        35: "Added onFailure: "block" for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that can?t start, times out, or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through"
    [Q3 964-972] ok
        Q3 present in docs-quotes.txt: True
        line 964 quoted: True
        line 965 quoted: True
        line 966 quoted: True
        line 967 quoted: True
        line 968 quoted: True
        line 969 quoted: True
        line 970 quoted: True
        line 971 quoted: True
        line 972 quoted: True

U17 (fact) So whenever the hook fires, a missing interpreter or script blocks every `git commit` through Claude until it is fixed, for example a hook command whose script path does not exist [E 29, E 35, Q3 966].
    [E 29] ok
        29: "Unless the hook is one whose failure blocks the action , a hook that can?t start is a non-blocking error too. When you set up a policy hook, watch for this notice on its first run, because a mistyped path in settings.json means the hook never runs. To block the action when the hook can?t start, set onFailure: "block" ."
    [E 35] ok
        35: "Added onFailure: "block" for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that can?t start, times out, or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through"
    [Q3 966] ok
        Q3 present in docs-quotes.txt: True
        line 966 quoted: True

U18 (fact) A missing Git Bash is different: then the hook does not fire at all (section 1) [Q2 1858-1859].
    [Q2 1858-1859] ok
        Q2 present in docs-quotes.txt: True
        line 1858 quoted: True
        line 1859 quoted: True

U19 (fact) The docs also say that on Windows without Git Bash, a shell-form `PreToolUse` command hook that fails with `onFailure` unset can block the tool call [E 78]; the Level 3 commit hook sets `onFailure` [settings 36].
    [E 78] ok
        78: "On Windows without Git Bash, a shell-form PreToolUse or PermissionRequest command hook that fails with onFailure unset can instead block the tool call ."
    [settings 36] ok
        36: "onFailure": "block",

U20 (fact) The scripts themselves exit 0 (go ahead), 2 (block, stderr goes back to Claude) or 1 (the project folder cannot be entered) [H tbc-commit-green, H tbc-commit-red, H tbc-could-not-cd].
    [H tbc-commit-green] ok
        ok 1 - tbc-commit-green

    [H tbc-commit-red] ok
        ok 3 - tbc-commit-red

    [H tbc-could-not-cd] ok

    [pack 283] ok

## 3. The git hook

U25 (fact) `.githooks/pre-commit` prints `pre-commit: ./mvnw -q verify`, runs `./mvnw -q verify` and aborts the commit when the build fails [pack 331-333, H githook-green-commit-goes-through, H githook-red-commit-aborted].
    [pack 331-333] ok
        331: #!/usr/bin/env sh
        332: echo "pre-commit: ./mvnw -q verify"
        333: ./mvnw -q verify || { echo "pre-commit: build failed, commit aborted" >&2; exit 1; }
    [H githook-green-commit-goes-through] ok
        ok 67 - githook-green-commit-goes-through
    [H githook-red-commit-aborted] ok
        ok 68 - githook-red-commit-aborted

U26 (fact) It runs only after `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, once per clone [pack 335, H githook-inactive-without-hooks-path], and `git commit --no-verify` skips it [H githook-skipped-by-no-verify].
    [pack 335] ok
        335: Activation (documented in the guide, run once per clone): `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.
    [H githook-inactive-without-hooks-path] ok
        ok 69 - githook-inactive-without-hooks-path
    [H githook-skipped-by-no-verify] ok
        ok 70 - githook-skipped-by-no-verify

U27 (fact) It is a `sh` script that calls the Unix wrapper `./mvnw`; `level-0-start` keeps `mvnw` and `.githooks/*` with LF line endings [pack 331, attributes].
    [pack 331] ok
        331: #!/usr/bin/env sh
    [attributes] ok
        level-0-start .gitattributes rules matching mvnw: mvnw text eol=lf
        level-0-start .gitattributes rules matching .githooks/pre-commit: .githooks/* text eol=lf

U28 (check) Whether Git for Windows runs it for a `git commit` typed outside Git Bash, for example in CMD, is not checked here (check W3).

## 4. What needs a Windows machine (manual checks for Maik)

U29 (check) W1: with Git for Windows, `git commit` through Claude Code runs the commit hook in Git Bash and a red build blocks it with exit code 2 and the stderr tail; this answers the pack's open point on the "shell Claude Code uses for hook commands there" [pack 327].
    [pack 327] ok
        327: shell Claude Code uses for hook commands there and document the result.

U30 (check) W2: without Git for Windows, the commit hook does not fire for a `git commit` that Claude runs [Q2 1858-1859].
    [Q2 1858-1859] ok
        Q2 present in docs-quotes.txt: True
        line 1858 quoted: True
        line 1859 quoted: True

U31 (check) W3: `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` makes Git for Windows run `.githooks/pre-commit` for a `git commit` typed in Git Bash and for one typed outside it, for example in CMD, and a red build aborts the commit.

## 6. Product findings

U36 (fact) PF-QA-T7-1 (from T7): pack line 283 and guide line 105 say a non-zero code other than 2 does not block; with `onFailure` set it does [pack 283, G 105, E 35].
    [pack 283] ok
        283: # Exit code 2 blocks the tool call and feeds stderr back to Claude. Any other non-zero code does NOT block.
    [G 105] ok
        105: Create `.claude/hooks/tests-before-commit.sh` (make it executable with `chmod +x`, and save it with LF line endings). It runs `./mvnw -q verify`; on failure it prints the last 40 lines to **stderr** and exits **2**, which blocks the commit and feeds the reason back to Claude. Any other non-zero exit code would NOT block.
    [E 35] ok
        35: "Added onFailure: "block" for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that can?t start, times out, or exits with an unexpected code blocks the action instead of letting it through"

U37 (fact) PF-T8-1: `tests-before-commit.sh` looks for `git commit` only up to the first double quote of the command, so a command with a double quote before `git commit` (escaped as `\"` in the JSON input), such as `cd "<folder>" && git commit -am wip`, exits 0 without a build [H tbc-escaped-quotes-before-commit].
    [H tbc-escaped-quotes-before-commit] ok
        ok 11 - tbc-escaped-quotes-before-commit
        #   tbc-escaped-quotes-before-commit | 0 | - | - | - | 0 | - | - | no | clean | 0

U38 (fact) PF-T8-2: plan feed-forward FF-T7-a asks this note to say that a missing Git Bash blocks every `git commit`; the docs and D9 say the hook does not fire without Git Bash [Q2 1858-1859, D9], so this note follows the docs (section 2).
    [Q2 1858-1859] ok
        Q2 present in docs-quotes.txt: True
        line 1858 quoted: True
        line 1859 quoted: True
    [D9] ok
        decisions.md section D9 present: True

U39 (fact) PF-T8-3: when `git ls-files` fails, `architecture-check-on-stop.sh` reads its empty output as "no untracked Java file" and exits 0 without the check [H acs-git-ls-files-fails].
    [H acs-git-ls-files-fails] ok
        ok 64 - acs-git-ls-files-fails

# Universal claims
N1 'every permission rule that runs a command is a Bash(...) rule': the permission rules in settings.json:
   Bash(./mvnw *) ; Bash(git status *) ; Bash(git diff *) ; Bash(git add *) ; Bash(git commit *) ; Read(./.env) ; Read(./.env.*) ; Bash(git push) ; Bash(git push *) ; Bash(* --no-verify*) ; Bash(git commit -n *)
   rules that are neither Bash(...) nor Read(...): none
N2 'Level 3 ships the bash hooks and the git pre-commit hook only': the level-3 manifest rows that stage a hook,
   and the files in level-3/files/dot-claude/hooks and level-3/files/dot-githooks:
   add | config | files/dot-claude/hooks/tests-before-commit.sh | .claude/hooks/tests-before-commit.sh | 755 | -
   add | config | files/dot-claude/hooks/architecture-check-on-stop.sh | .claude/hooks/architecture-check-on-stop.sh | 755 | -
   add | config | files/dot-githooks/pre-commit | .githooks/pre-commit | 755 | -
   dot-claude/hooks: architecture-check-on-stop.sh tests-before-commit.sh
   dot-githooks: pre-commit
N3 'level-0-start keeps mvnw and .githooks/* with LF': the attributes tag above lists every rule of the
   level-0-start .gitattributes that matches mvnw or .githooks/pre-commit; each one sets eol=lf.
